title: Heterogeneous Region Peering vs PrivateLink - POC Scoping

Customer to provide representative request traces and dataset sample
Schedule in-region pilot window (proposed week of 2026-03-02)
Redwood to send security enclave docs and PrivateLink architecture diagram
action_items: Alex Turner: Share bench matrix, quant profiles and cost estimates (due 2026-02-18)

summary: Discovery and scoping call for a Private Networking POC. Discussed tradeoffs between VPC peering and PrivateLink for cross-region residency, defined success metrics (latency SLOs, throughput, data residency proof), collected workload sizing, and agreed on benchmark matrix and pilot timeline.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-02-13 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 53 minutes
- Recording: yes
- Attendees: Alex Turner (AE, Redwood), Samira Patel (SE, Redwood), Diego Ramos (Redwood), Maya Chen (Platform Eng, Mariner), Jon Alvarez (Cloud Arch), Priya Nair (Security), Liam O'Reilly (SRE), Sara Bennett (Product)

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving time. I'm Alex, I'm the AE on this account, Samira and Diego from our engineering team will cover the technical bits. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Maya: Maya here.
[00:12] Jon: Jon.
[00:14] Priya: Priya.
[00:16] Liam: Liam.
[00:18] Sara: Sara.
[00:20] Alex: Great. Our goal for today is to scope a POC for private networking + residency constraints — specifically options between V P C peering and PrivateLink across two regions, plus egress restrictions. We'll capture success criteria, size the workload, and agree a benchmark plan and timeline.

[02:05] Samira (SE): Quick context from Redwood: our Private offering can run in a customer VPC or via PrivateLink endpoints; peering gives you direct L3 routing but you need cross-region peering topology, PrivateLink gives endpoint isolation and less routing exposure but can add NAT/egress hops depending on your design. Also mention that for some clouds peering across regions has limits and costs.
[02:35] Jon: Right, our main constraint is data residency — PHI-derived tokens can't leave region eu-west-1. We have two workloads: realtime triage (low latency, lots of small requests) and nightly batch embeddings for analytics (high throughput, larger payloads).
[03:10] Samira: Good. Can you give numbers for QPS and payload sizes?
[03:18] Liam: Realtime is about 120 requests/sec at peak, average payload 1.2KB, 95th token latency target is 250ms. Nightly batch is roughly 1.2M records, each embedding payload ~6KB, want to finish within 3 hours.
[03:45] Diego: That helps. For the realtime path we usually recommend colocating inference in the same region as origin traffic to meet latency SLOs. If you need cross-region forwarding, we need to test cold KV cache impacts.
[04:12] Priya: Security question — all data must stay in eu-west-1. We can't have sensitive content egress to other regions, including transient caching. Also we need KMS integration with customer-managed keys and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[04:40] Samira: Understood. Redwood supports customer KMS for Private deployments; we can keep logs local and ship via your Fluentd to the SIEM. We'll share our audit log schema doc after the call.

[06:00] Alex: Let's enumerate success criteria so we can mark the POC pass/fail. Maya, what would a successful pilot look like from Mariner's PM/Risk perspective?
[06:20] Maya: Two things: first, proof that inference for PHI-bound requests never leaves eu-west-1 at any point (including fallback behavior). Second, meet the latency SLO: 95th <250ms for realtime at 120 qps. Third, cost estimate within X of baseline — I'd like a ballpark.
[06:48] Sara: And from product, reliability is key — 99.9% availability during pilot window and predictable autoscaling behavior for spikes.
[07:05] Alex: So success criteria recap: residency proof (no cross-region egress), latency 95th <250ms at 120qps steady, nightly batch completion under 3 hours, availability target 99.9. We'll add an architecture sign-off step for Priya.

[08:30] Samira: For architecture options: Option A — regional deployment with VPC peering between mariner-prod-eu and redwood-private-eu. Advantages: lower network hops, direct routing for KV cache; Disadvantages: cross-account peering setups and peering across regions can be limited. Option B — PrivateLink / interface endpoints where traffic goes to an endpoint service in eu-west-1; Advantage: no routing changes and tighter control over allowed principals; Disadvantage: often requires NAT or extra ALBs for egress and may add 10-25ms overhead depending on path.
[09:12] Jon: Can PrivateLink be configured so that fallback models also stay in-region? Our fallback policy currently points to a lower-capacity variant hosted in another region.
[09:22] Samira: Yes, we can pin fallback variants to the same region in your Private deployment. If you use our hosted multi-region model, then we have to route to the closest compatible variant — which we avoid for this pilot.
[09:40] Priya: What about encryption in transit between your infra and our VPC endpoints? We need mTLS and customer-specified certs.
[09:50] Diego: We support TLS with mutual auth for PrivateLink and VPC peering endpoints, and you can plug in your own certs — we'll share the exact cert exchange runbook.

[11:05] Maya: Benchmarks — what's the plan? We want reproducible tests and scripts we control.
[11:18] Samira: Proposed benchmark matrix:
- Realtime latency: run synthetic load at 50%, 100%, 150% of target QPS (60, 120, 180) with 95th/99th latency reported, p50/p95 CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost per request.
- KV cache warm vs cold: measure latency impact for cold-start sequences vs warmed KV cache for a set of prompts.
- Nightly batch: run embedding jobs with realistic payloads, measure throughput and end-to-end time.
- Egress proof checks: packet-level traceroutes and tiled flow logs to demonstrate no cross-region NATs.

[12:05] Liam: For realtime we'll need an xfer of traces so the script can replay real traffic distribution — we'll provide an abridged 48h sample.
[12:15] Samira: Great. We'll provide a k6/locust script and a kubernetes job for the batch test and a step-by-step runbook. Expect a bench results spreadsheet with tabs for each permutation.

[13:40] Jon: For multi-region things — we actually have user traffic coming from eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. The residency rule applies to eu-west-1 only for PHI. Can we create routing rules that keep PHI in west and allow non-PHI to cross to central?
[13:58] Alex: Yes — we recommend a routing policy with token-tagging at the edge that marks PHI tokens and enforces route-to-local region policy for those. We'll help instrument that with an edge lambda or ingress rule.
[14:20] Priya: That requires token-level deterministic marking. Is Redwood able to accept a header that indicates PHI classification and treat it as the source of truth?
[14:28] Samira: We can. We'll also recommend an in-flight verification step to confirm classification using a hash or signed header to avoid accidental leaks.

[16:00] Diego: On sizing — our rough capacity assumptions: for 120 qps with 1.2KB payloads, depending on the model size, you'd need between 1-3 gpus for realtime in an optimized quantized setup; batch embedding of 1.2M rows could run on a 4 GPU pool in parallel to hit the 3 hour window. But these numbers change with exact model and sequence length.
[16:35] Maya: We're planning to use a smaller open model to start, then move to a tuned mid-sized model. We'll share model name and typical token lengths by tomorrow.

[18:00] Alex: Costs — Diego, can you summarize expected incremental network and inference cost delta between peering and PrivateLink?
[18:10] Diego: Roughly: peering usually has lower per-request network egress charges but can incur cross-region peering fees. PrivateLink typically charges per-hour per-endpoint plus data processed; adds a bit more latency than peering. We'll provide an estimated cost table once we have exact traffic numbers.

[19:50] Samira: Edge cases: what happens during overload/fallback? If primary region saturates, we can fail open to a non-PHI safe region but Priya you said PHI can't leave; so we'll need a strict fallback that returns 429s for PHI rather than rerouting. We'll set that as a safety policy for the POC.
[20:22] Priya: Yes, we require fail-closed for PHI. Non-PHI can use fail-open to maintain availability.

[22:00] Maya: Timeline — we want a 3-week pilot window with 1 week of setup + 1 week of steady-state benchmark + a final week for analysis and sign-off. Is that feasible?
[22:15] Alex: Feasible. Proposed timeline: week of 2026-03-02 provision infra and verify connectivity, week of 2026-03-09 run benchmarks, week of 2026-03-16 analyze and review. We can compress but need at least one full benchmark week.
[22:38] Sara: We also want a short canary run before the main benchmark to validate instrumentation.
[22:44] Samira: We'll include a 24h canary step in the runbook.

[25:00] Jon: For evidence of residency, what artifacts will Redwood provide?
[25:10] Diego: We'll produce: 1) network flow logs showing 0 cross-region destinations for PHI-marked flows, 2) audit log snapshot showing key wrap/unwrap in your KMS in-region, 3) benchmark CSVs and raw traces, 4) a short reproducible script to run the same checks.
[25:45] Priya: Need the KMS proof to include envelope key IDs and timestamps.
[25:52] Diego: Yep, we'll include that in the audit export.

[28:30] Samira: Risk register quick hits: possible surprises are inter-region peering limits in your cloud account, NAT egress from PrivateLink endpoints if not carefully placed, and cold KV cache penalties. We'll run a preflight to enumerate account limits and request you grant us a read-only view so we can check quotas.
[29:05] Maya: We'll grant a limited role to the Redwood pilots team for the preflight check.

[31:00] Alex: Any competing solutions you're considering?
[31:08] Sara: We looked at OtherCloudAI and Infralabs. OtherCloudAI is simpler but doesn't offer same observability; Infralabs has tight VPC integration but higher cost.
[31:25] Alex: Noted. We'll highlight where Redwood provides auditability and cost controls.

[33:00] Samira: Operational runbook items: how to rotate keys, how to escalate on SLO breach, and who to call for on-call. We'll supply an escalation matrix and an SLO alerting playbook.
[33:25] Liam: On-call: Mariner owns application on-call, Redwood provides a SE on-call for the pilot windows.

[35:00] Diego: Quick tech note: KV cache semantics — if we co-locate cache in-region we get much better tail latencies. Cold cache hits for long sequences can add 80-180ms to p95. We should test warm vs cold patterns matching real traffic.
[35:25] Maya: Our traffic has a 30% repeat prompt pattern, so warming will help. We'll annotate traces with that distribution.

[38:00] Alex: Documentation handoffs: we'll send three artifacts after this call — bench matrix + scripts (link), Private connectivity runbook (link), and security/audit checklist (link). We'll also include estimated costs.
[38:20] Diego: Links: short bench doc https://go.redwood/bench/mariner-2026 (placeholder), security checklist https://go.redwood/security/mariner (placeholder).

[40:00] Jon: Any limitations on model families you support in Private mode? We use a custom quantized variant.
[40:10] Samira: We support a broad set of model families; for Private deployments we can run custom quantized weights, though we need to validate kernel compatibility. That validation step is part of onboarding and usually takes 48-72 hours.

[42:00] Priya: Compliance question: do you have SOC2 and ISO attestations we can include in our vendor review?
[42:08] Alex: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified — we'll send the cert pack and point to our external audit report.

[44:00] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps verbally so nothing is missed.
[44:06] Alex: I'll start: Redwood to share bench scripts, runbook, security pack and cost estimate by 2026-02-18.
[44:16] Maya: Mariner to upload traces and list of models/token profiles by 2026-02-20.
[44:25] Samira: Redwood to run preflight account quota check after receiving read-only role, due 2026-02-24.
[44:35] Diego: We'll also propose final pilot dates by end of next week.

[46:00] Priya: One more thing — we need an NDA addendum for the pilot to cover PHI handling.
[46:08] Alex: We'll loop in legal and send the addendum draft today.

[48:00] Sara: Thanks everyone this is useful.
[48:05] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifact bundle.

[50:00] End recording.

Notes on transcription: some speaker overlaps and casing errors; 'VPC' sometimes transcribed as 'V P C', 'KV cache' sometimes as 'K V cash', 'PrivateLink' appears as 'Private Link' in parts.
